note: Peer beats (SocGen/BNP, item 0) support LCL NII but a 17-analyst mega-cap that pre-released its quarter in an October pre-close note and fell on 6 of 9 results days leaves almost nothing unpriced; FICC risk (item 1) offsets.

The July guide never mentioned energy and Iberian power has since more than doubled year on year with Aperam quantifying ~EUR20m of EBITDA a quarter (item 0), nickel has kept falling into the Q4 surcharge line (item 1) and the closest peer says European demand is still low (item 2); Acerinox gives a next-quarter guide every quarter and that guide is what moved this stock +10.7% in July.

Vinmonopolet's own through-September file (item 0) puts Q3 Norwegian monopoly volumes below the 2-3% decline the one published preview assumes, and the Vara consensus of 19.1 sits above Inderes's 18.0 with a +7.5% run-up into a 'reduce' rating and a negative Q4 cost-inflation message (item 3).

Nordic power prices doubling (item 0) should lift Renewables but it is a public daily series the three analysts model, and the 8% consensus EPS cut already prices the Wind Service comp (item 1); nothing here is unpriced and the observed results-day median is 1.78%.

The CFO has publicly deferred the NII guidance refinement to year-end (item 0), which is exactly the non-upgrade the stock fell 7.1% on in July, and every Spanish bank that has printed this fortnight has been sold on in-line numbers (item 3: Bankinter -7.6%, Santander -5.6%, BBVA -5%); a habitual profit beat (item 2) has not helped this name before.

Four of five Polish banks beat the PAP bar this week on the same line (provisions below forecast, item 0) and Erste BP beat Q2 by 11.3% on that line, with no Q3 Art. 17 CHF report filed (item 1) and the O-SII cut to quantify (item 2); the +7.3% five-day run-up prices much of the sector read, so the residual is modest.

Under the DPLTA the minority share is paid a contractually fixed EUR1.28 Ausgleich confirmed final on 1 October, so the Q3 numbers cannot change what the share is worth: realised vol is 0.27% a day and every results day this year moved under 0.7%. An honest zero.

The company's own published Vara consensus already sits at the bottom of the guide on margin and outside it on cash (item 1), needing H2 EBITDA of 223-255m against a Q2 run-rate of 102m, while the stock has run +15.4% with no identifiable catalyst to a 52-week high and above 13 of 15 broker targets with shorts covering (item 2) - the bar in the price is above the bar in the consensus, and a narrowing to the low end can still be sold on a 45%-vol name.

Waertsilae's Q3 service sales -2% (item 0) says the aftermarket drag management expected to improve in H2 has not, against a rich unverified consensus margin; strong newbuild contracting (item 1) offsets, and with the bar unsourced every size is capped.

An easy Q3 organic comparison with record US margins and the last two EBITA beats both paying +4.3% (item 0), plus FX turning from headwind to neutral (item 1), against a consensus SEB says already has the margin at the top of the 12-14% target (item 2); no Q3 consensus was found, so everything is capped small.

The line the move lives on - whether the H2 project-sale guide holds, firms or slips (item 2) - has no direction in any source, so the size is large and the sign is nearly neutral; the Norwegian data-centre halt and tax proposals (item 0) reach this window only through management's commentary, and insiders bought above spot (item 1).

The two freshest findings cancel: an inferred HELG transition gain of NOK 124-140m (item 0, a one-off below operating income and an accounting inference) against associate income down ~50m QoQ published in SMN's report this morning (item 1); fifteen observed results days have a 1.43% median move.

A beat on company-compiled consensus is near-certain (item 0) and almost entirely expected, while FY consensus already sits above the guide so a raise to it is a non-event (item 1, the Q1-26 pattern that cost -3.35%) and Lloyds fell 5.3% today on 2027 NII colour NatWest has yet to give (item 2); the two sides very nearly offset.

The mechanical guidance raise (item 0) is public arithmetic that Jefferies said out loud three weeks ago and the stock has already run +7% into it, and this name sold its last raise-and-beat 8.95%; Merck's Enflonsia +138% today (item 2) points at Beyfortus share loss in the stocking quarter.

A release that the 21 October warning itself promised would carry 'further updates', on a 96%-vol name eight days after a -23.9% day, so the size is the largest on the day and the sign is close to a coin: an arguably overdone reaction and visible bottom-fishing (items 0-2) against an unquantified structural Philippines hit (item 4), a likely Ukraine impairment (item 6) and JPMorgan AM adding to its short on every reported day through the rebound (item 5).

Q3 is the first test of an FY guide needing EURm 20-25 in H2 after a 26% Q2 EBITDA miss (item 0), and guidance decisions move this name 5-10%; Netcompany raising its low end this morning (item 1) is a real positive read on the public-sector half, so the direction stays close to even.

The leverage step from 4.4x to about 5x on a weak quarter (item 1) is arithmetic nobody has published, on top of the only sourced bar being a broker preview of EBITDA -34.6% (item 0); the unvalued EDF EPR2 award the day before the print (item 3) is the one thing that could be quantified upward, and eight of this name's last prints averaged small moves.

Q3 Euribor averaged well above Q2 and the July NII guide of +Low-Mid SD only partly embeds it, leaving room for a nudge (item 0); unlike CaixaBank this name has risen on five of its last six results days, so the sector's sell-the-print reaction function (item 1) is a weaker argument here.
